startup.name: Unisson
startup.one_liner: AI agents that automate B2B software implementation
startup.description: AI subject matter experts for customer success, implementation and sales engineering teams at B2B software companies. The agents learn a product in about 20 minutes, work in Slack, text or email, gather requirements from existing tools and handle onboarding, health audits, product administration and custom integrations. Pays: per team or per agent subscription from software vendors that have large implementation backlogs.

yc_acceptance.basis: The input file places Unisson in the Winter 2026 batch with the batch start as the as_of date, so acceptance is treated as already happened. The prior for a random applicant is about 1 percent (references/yc_acceptance.md), but conditional on being listed in the batch the residual doubt is only data error or a deferral. Seed odds below are conditional on being in YC.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: The only way the YC step fails here is a clerical error in the batch listing or a deferral to a later batch. Unisson was reported in the batch directory as of the as_of date, so the reason to say no has already been resolved in its favor.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --calibration-only --industry B2B --years 2022-2025 (150 researched: seed 49% / 59% / 65%, series_a cond 26% n=74, series_b cond 16% n=19); seed cond known-only 59% (n=126); months_to_seed median 7 (p25 3, p75 15) from knowledge/tables/time_to_milestones.csv calibration sample
anchors.adjustment_reason: The anchor is the 59 percent ever rate for B2B 2022 to 2025. The window is only 10 months from the Winter 2026 batch start and the median time to seed is 7 months with p75 of 15, so about 55 to 60 percent of eventual seed raisers have raised by month 10, giving about 0.34. A two person AI native team gets no lift, because the winners test showed hot sector lifts did not separate winners, and I stay under the 1.25 times cap.

bands.rationale: Small post YC round of $1M to $3M, typically angels and a micro fund. This is the second most common outcome for a 2 to 5 person team with early pilots and no scaled revenue, and it is more likely here than in the winners test sample because press favours big rounds. The plain YC deal of about $500K does not count as seed in this forecast.
Institutional seed of $3M to $6M led by a seed fund. This is the center of the 2022 and later benchmark (median about $4.1M in our table) and of the 2026 confirmed raises (lower quartile $4.3M).

Larger institutional seed of $6M to $12M. Reachable if a design partner or demo produces competitive tension, as in the 2026 winners where the median confirmed raise was $6.0M, a sample that leans high.
Upside seed above $12M, reserved for a hot category with a standout team. Rare for a team this small and early.

ladder.why_it_fails: Unisson most likely misses a seed because two founders with a horizontal agent that can do many tasks have to prove depth in one workflow. The closest YC peers sero and onboard-io from 2022 are still alive without big rounds, and lume was acquired after a seed. Investors in 2026 see many AI SME and implementation agents, and want revenue from named customers within months, which a two person team may not have by the time they raise.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --calibration-only --industry B2B --years 2022-2025 (150 researched: seed 49% / 59% / 65%, series_a cond 26% n=74, series_b cond 16% n=19); series_a cond 26% (n=74) (ever); months_to_series_a median 29 from batch start (B2B 2022 to 2025, n=19)
anchors.adjustment_reason: A Series A within 10 months of the batch, and after a seed, is very rare: the B2B median time from batch to A is 29 months (n=19). The ever conditional rate is 26 percent, and the window cuts that to about 0.03.

bands.rationale: Thin or small Series A, close to a large seed, for a company with some revenue but unproven repeatability. Current 2022 and later YC Series A lower quartile is $10.0M, so this is the thin end.
Typical Series A of $9M to $18M, matching the 2022 and later YC median of $14.15M (n=52) and public market medians near $17M.
Upside Series A with a clear ARR ramp; AI native companies have printed larger A rounds in 2025 and 2026 but these remain the minority.

ladder.why_it_fails: An A in this window needs a seed already raised in the first months and revenue near $1M annualized, which an implementation agent product has rarely reached within a year. Buyers are customer success leaders who run long pilots, and trust is a barrier before agents touch customer data. The likely path is a seed, then a long slog to repeatable revenue.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --calibration-only --industry B2B --years 2022-2025: series_b cond 16% (n=19) ever, lower 2% known-only
anchors.adjustment_reason: The window is 10 months, and Series B needs a median of 46 months from batch start (all eras, n=510 in time_to_milestones.csv; B2B 2022 to 2025 median 26 months on n=3, right censored). The probability is a floor for a fast outlier, far below the 16 percent ever rate, because only a company that raised both a seed and an A inside the window can get here.

bands.rationale: Thin Series B or extension, near the 2022 and later lower quartile of $25M.
Typical Series B, around the YC 2022 and later median of $37M (n=22).
Upside Series B on breakout growth, in line with the few 2022 and later B valuations near $775M.

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series B within 10 months is effectively a tail event that needs two earlier rounds in a few months. The floor reflects only an extraordinary growth story. Even beyond the window, a B would need Unisson to prove it is the deployment layer for B2B software across many products, which is harder than a narrow workflow. Neighbors such as sero and onboard-io did not get past seed, so the likely end is a stall at the A step or a small acquisition.

anchors.source: Series C cond is 0% of n=3 in the B2B 2022 to 2025 cohort; the older all-era calibration sample gives about 30 to 35 percent of series_b reaching C, discounted here for the window
anchors.adjustment_reason: The window ends 10 months after the as_of date and a Series C needs a median of 61 months from batch start (all eras, n=221 in time_to_milestones.csv). The probability is a small floor rather than an anchor ratio, because 3 companies in the recent cohort cannot support a rate.

bands.rationale: Series C or growth round near the 2022 and later YC median of $45M (n=9), with a flat or modest step up.
Typical growth round of $80M to $150M for a category leader with strong net retention, as seen in the larger 2022 and later rounds in the YC data.
Upside round for a category winner; the sample of 2022 and later C rounds is tiny (n=9) so this band is judgment.

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series C within 10 months is essentially impossible given round timing, so the number is a floor and not a forecast. Beyond the window a late stage round would require tens of millions in recurring revenue from implementation agents, a scale that no recent YC peer in this wedge has shown. Lume was acquired after seed, so the realistic tail is acquisition rather than growth rounds.

outcomes.why_it_fails: Most failures are a stall at the pilot stage or a pivot, because the product is horizontal, the buyer segment is small and the big platforms and the fast followers copy it. Lume from the same wedge was acquired at seed stage, a typical good outcome here, and a venture scale win would need a repeatable deployment engine that the founders have not shown.

killers.risk: Pilot purgatory: customer success buyers try the agent but never move it to production access
killers.evidence: Agents need admin level access to customer products, which security reviews slow; neighbors in the YC data stayed small.
killers.mitigation: Land one workflow such as onboarding audits with measured hours saved.

killers.risk: Horizontal positioning without depth: any product agent is generic
killers.evidence: The description lists audits, onboarding, administration and integrations, a broad scope for two founders.
killers.mitigation: Pick one vertical class of software and one task.

killers.risk: Fast follower and platform copy: Salesforce, ServiceNow and Slack agents absorb the use case
killers.evidence: Agent features are being added to suites and to chat tools that already hold the context.
killers.mitigation: Build integrations and a knowledge base that suites do not offer.

killers.risk: Two person team runs out of time before revenue shows
killers.evidence: Team size 2 from the input; many YC teams of two raise a seed only after showing revenue.
killers.mitigation: Show paid pilots by demo day.

technical_complexity.rationale: Agents that learn to use any product in 20 minutes means computer use, documentation reading and tool integration with high reliability needs. A two person team can ship a narrow demo, but general reliability across arbitrary products is hard and a dependency on frontier models.

who: OpenAI and Anthropic computer use agents
takeover_risk.rationale: Large platforms already add agents inside customer success and support suites, and model labs offer computer use. A rival could ship a similar agent for implementation in about 9 months using the same models.

A YC graduate reported a $4M seed for AI agents handling software onboarding and retention.

brand.rationale: Unisson is a pronounceable coined variant of unison, in line with other invented YC names, but it does not hint at agents or implementation. A neutral name does not change the ladder.

narrative.headline: Unisson is a two person team in a crowded agent category with a short window, so a seed is possible but not likely, and the odds do not rank it.
narrative.general_summary: Unisson sells AI subject matter experts to customer success and implementation teams. The wedge is real, with peers that raised seeds, but older YC peers sero and onboard-io raised little and lume was acquired. With only 10 months from the batch start to the judging date and a two person team, the seed is about a third likely and a Series A is a floor. A seed if reached is most likely $3M to $6M, and the success path needs one workflow with measurable savings.

assumptions: Window is 10 months from 2026-01-05 to 2026-11-17; seed means above about $1M from outside investors, excluding the YC deal.
Tags field is empty and team size is 2 from the input.
